channel.description: This is a randomly ordered feed of the most recent entries from summarizedStoriesMainNLscienceAndDiscovery, skipping any feeds with errors.

item.title: School-bus-sized 'terror croc' that ate dinosaurs returns
item.description: A massive crocodilian capable of attacking dinosaurs has been recreated as the first scientifically accurate mounted skeleton of Deinosuchus.

item.title: Stanford scientists find immune cells that explode like bombs
item.description: Stanford researchers discovered immune cells in flatworms that explode within minutes, killing nearby bacteria and foreign cells before vanishing completely.

item.title: Brain cells identified that sustain motivation during challenging tasks
item.description: Orexin neurons appear to help maintain effort when rewards become harder to obtain. Blocking their activity may reduce persistence.

item.title: Fossilized snake brain from 80 million years ago reveals unexpected diversity
item.description: A well-preserved snake fossil from Brazil indicates early snakes were more varied than previously believed. Detailed brain reconstruction offers new insights.
